# Configure Boundary OIDC authentication with Auth0

Boundary delegates authentication to [Auth0](https://auth0.com) using the [OIDC (OpenID Connect) auth method](/boundary/docs/domain-model/auth-methods#oidc-auth-method-attributes), a common single sign-on (SSO) integration. Registering Boundary as an Auth0 application takes two steps: configure the application in Auth0, then create the matching OIDC auth method in Boundary.

## Prerequisites

- An Auth0 account. HashiCorp recommends using a test account that is not tied to another SSO method.
- Administrator access to Boundary.

## Create an Auth0 application

Registering Boundary as an application in Auth0 lets Auth0 authenticate Boundary users and redirect them back to Boundary after a successful login.

1. In the Auth0 dashboard, select **Applications**, and then select **Create Application**.
1. Select **Regular Web Application**, name the application, and select **Create**.
1. From the application's **Settings** tab, scroll to **Application URIs**.
1. Under **Allowed Callback URLs**, add the following URL, replacing `BOUNDARY_ADDR` with the address of your Boundary controller:

   ```plaintext
   https://BOUNDARY_ADDR/v1/auth-methods/oidc:authenticate:callback
   ```

1. Under **Allowed Logout URLs**, add your Boundary address:

   ```plaintext
   https://BOUNDARY_ADDR
   ```

1. Select **Save Changes**.
1. From the top of the **Settings** tab, record the following values. You need them to create the OIDC auth method in Boundary:

   - **Domain**: maps to the auth method's `issuer` attribute.
   - **Client ID**: maps to the auth method's `client-id` attribute.
   - **Client Secret**: maps to the auth method's `client-secret` attribute.

<Note>

The Boundary `issuer` value must have a trailing `/` at the end of the Auth0 domain, for example `https://YOUR_DOMAIN.auth0.com/`. If you omit the trailing slash, Boundary cannot validate the auth method's configuration against the Auth0 discovery document.

</Note>

Any Auth0 user assigned to the application can authenticate to Boundary. Refer to the [Auth0 user management documentation](https://auth0.com/docs/manage-users) to create and assign users.

## Create an OIDC auth method for Auth0

<Tabs>
<Tab heading="UI" group="ui">

1. Log in to Boundary.
1. Select the scope in which you want to create the auth method.
1. Select **Auth Methods**, then select **New**.
1. Select **OIDC**, and complete the following fields:
   - **Name**: (Optional) An optional name for identification purposes.
   - **Description**: (Optional) An optional description of the auth method.
   - **Issuer**: (Required) The Auth0 application's **Domain**, including a trailing `/`.
   - **Client ID**: (Required) The Auth0 application's **Client ID**.
   - **Client Secret**: (Required) The Auth0 application's **Client Secret**.
   - **API URL Prefix**: (Required) The address where your Boundary controller is reachable by Auth0, for example `https://BOUNDARY_ADDR`.
1. Select **Save**.
1. Select **Edit Form**, scroll to **Signing Algorithms**, add `RS256`, and select **Add**.
1. Select **Save**.

</Tab>
<Tab heading="CLI" group="cli">

```shell-session
$ boundary auth-methods create oidc \
  -issuer "https://YOUR_DOMAIN.auth0.com/" \
  -client-id "$CLIENT_ID" \
  -client-secret "$CLIENT_SECRET" \
  -signing-algorithm RS256 \
  -api-url-prefix "https://BOUNDARY_ADDR" \
  -name "auth0"
```

The `issuer`, `client-id`, and `client-secret` values come from the Auth0 application settings. The `api-url-prefix` must match the address where your Boundary controller is reachable by Auth0.

Refer to the [auth-methods create](/boundary/docs/commands/auth-methods/create) command documentation for additional fields that you can use when you create OIDC auth methods.

</Tab>
<Tab heading="Terraform" group="terraform">

Apply the following Terraform configuration:

```hcl
resource "boundary_auth_method_oidc" "provider" {
  name               = "Auth0"
  description        = "OIDC auth method for Auth0"
  scope_id           = "global"
  issuer             = "https://YOUR_DOMAIN.auth0.com/"
  client_id          = "CLIENT_ID"
  client_secret      = "CLIENT_SECRET"
  signing_algorithms = ["RS256"]
  api_url_prefix     = "https://BOUNDARY_ADDR"
}
```

Replace `scope_id`, `issuer`, `client_id`, `client_secret`, and `api_url_prefix` with the values for your scope and Auth0 application.

Refer to the [boundary_auth_method_oidc](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/boundary/latest/docs/resources/auth_method_oidc) resource documentation for additional fields that you can use when you create OIDC auth methods.

</Tab>
</Tabs>

## Troubleshooting

#### `oidc: issuer did not match the issuer returned by provider`

If you omit the trailing `/` from the Auth0 domain, activating the auth method fails with an error similar to the following:

<CodeBlockConfig hideClipboard>

```plaintext
oidc: issuer did not match the issuer returned by provider, expected "https://YOUR_DOMAIN.auth0.com" got "https://YOUR_DOMAIN.auth0.com/"
```

</CodeBlockConfig>

Update the auth method's `issuer` attribute to include the trailing `/`, and try again.

## More information

- Refer to the [Auth method](/boundary/docs/domain-model/auth-methods#oidc-auth-method-attributes) domain model topic for the full list of OIDC auth method attributes.
- Refer to [Filter managed groups](/boundary/docs/rbac/users/managed-groups) to assign roles to Auth0 users based on claims returned by Auth0, such as group membership.
- Refer to the [Auth0 documentation](https://auth0.com/docs) for information about configuring Auth0 applications, rules, and custom claims.
